nodes.label: Denario: Deep Knowledge AI Agents for Scientific Discovery
nodes.author: Francisco Villaescusa-Navarro, Boris Bolliet, Pablo Villanueva-Domingo, et al.
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent AI system for end-to-end scientific research; modular architecture with Idea, Literature, Methods, Analysis, Paper, and Review modules; demonstrates capability across 13 scientific disciplines with expert evaluation of generated papers.

nodes.label: Denario Modular Architecture
nodes.rationale: Idea module generates research concepts; Literature module checks existing work; Methods module develops research plans; Analysis module writes and executes code; Paper module drafts scientific papers; Review module provides peer feedback; enables task-specific optimization and end-to-end research workflows.

nodes.label: Cmbagent Deep-Research Backend
nodes.rationale: Deep-research backend enabling end-to-end scientific analysis; orchestrates multiple modules for complex research tasks; supports interdisciplinary work combining methods from quantum physics, machine learning, and astrophysics.

nodes.label: Interdisciplinary Knowledge Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Denario excels at combining ideas from different disciplines; demonstrated by paper applying quantum physics and machine learning methods to astrophysical data; reflects growing interdisciplinarity of modern research.

nodes.label: AI-Driven Scientific Discovery
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent systems performing end-to-end research workflows: idea generation, literature review, methodology development, analysis, paper writing, peer review; raises questions about epistemic changes, scientific work structure, and philosophy of science in AI-driven research.

nodes.label: Denario AI Multi-Agent Research System
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent framework designed to assist in all stages of scientific research, from idea generation through paper writing and review

nodes.label: Idea Generation Module

nodes.label: Literature Review Module
nodes.rationale: Checks literature to determine novelty of ideas using Semantic Scholar or FutureHouse Owl

nodes.label: Methodology Development Module
nodes.rationale: Develops detailed research plans and methodologies to execute project ideas

nodes.label: Analysis Execution Module

nodes.label: Paper Writing Module
nodes.rationale: Writes scientific papers with sections, citations, and formatted output

nodes.label: Paper Review Module
nodes.rationale: Reviews generated papers and provides referee reports on strengths and weaknesses

nodes.label: AG2 Agent Framework
nodes.rationale: Open-source AgentOS supporting advanced agentic AI applications with conversation programming

nodes.label: LangGraph Orchestration Framework
nodes.rationale: Python framework for orchestrating agents through directed graphs with dynamic flow control

nodes.label: Planning & Control Orchestration Strategy

nodes.label: Plan Reviewer Agent

nodes.rationale: Well-known issue where LLMs generate incorrect code, unsupported conclusions, or fabricated information

nodes.label: Denario Advantages
nodes.rationale: Benefits including enhanced researcher capabilities, rapid shallow research, transparency, interdisciplinary connections, exploration of risky ideas, and time savings for deeper thinking

nodes.label: Denario Limitations
nodes.rationale: Issues with citations, depth of explanations, LaTeX formatting, and code execution reliability

nodes.label: Ethics: Quality of Research
nodes.rationale: Risk that generative AI tools enable production of large numbers of low-quality papers and artificial inflation of research output

nodes.label: Ethics: Scientific Training and Education
nodes.rationale: Questions about value of scientific writing and data analysis skills when AI tools can automate these tasks

nodes.label: Ethics: Quality and Legitimacy Assessment
nodes.rationale: Risk of trusting AI-generated results without validation; questions about who defines quality and correctness

nodes.label: Ethics: Homogenization of Research
nodes.rationale: Concern that AI agents may bias research toward confirming existing literature, stifling innovation

nodes.label: Ethics: Access and Democratization
nodes.rationale: Computational infrastructure requirements create barriers to access; affects which fields and problems are tackled

nodes.label: Ethics: Authorship and Credit
nodes.rationale: Debates over professional credit allocation, responsibility for results, and accountability when AI systems are used

nodes.label: Ethics: Misalignment of Publishing Incentives
nodes.rationale: Career incentives for publication volume may lead to deluge of low-quality papers and self-citation abuse

nodes.label: Ethics: Environmental Concerns
nodes.rationale: Training and running LLMs consume significant energy, water, and rare earth materials at unsustainable scale

nodes.label: Ethics: Malicious Use
nodes.rationale: AI agents could flood literature with politically or commercially motivated claims, potentially laundering false information

nodes.label: Responsible Usage of Denario
nodes.rationale: Under responsible usage, Denario can improve research quality by freeing researcher time for deeper thinking and validation

nodes.label: Irresponsible Usage of Denario
nodes.rationale: Generating papers without validation will degrade research quality given current system capabilities

nodes.source_location: Section A.13 Quantum physics, deep learning and cosmology
nodes.rationale: Novel approach leveraging Quantum-Inspired Tensor Trains on multi-scale substructure features with learned topological embeddings for cosmological parameter estimation from dark matter halo merger trees

nodes.label: K-Means Clustering for Water State Identification
nodes.rationale: Unsupervised clustering to objectively identify emergent interfacial water states based on structural features

nodes.rationale: Interpretable gradient boosting regressor with SHapley Additive exPlanations to quantify influence of system design parameters on water diffusion

nodes.label: Robust Linear Regression with Huber Loss
nodes.rationale: Mitigates influence of outlier galaxies on fitting by using Huber loss function, less sensitive to extreme values than ordinary least squares

nodes.label: Bootstrap Resampling for Uncertainty Estimation
nodes.rationale: Generates 1000 bootstrap samples to estimate uncertainty distributions for fitted parameters, reporting median and 68% confidence intervals

nodes.label: Hierarchical Linear Modeling
nodes.rationale: Accounts for nested structure of data and allows varying relationships across catalogs or mass bins while partially pooling information

nodes.label: Random Forest and Gradient Boosted Trees
nodes.rationale: Ensemble methods to capture non-linear relationships and complex interactions between input parameters and output relation properties

nodes.label: Permutation Feature Importance
nodes.rationale: Model-agnostic technique measuring decrease in model performance when feature values are randomly shuffled to assess importance

nodes.label: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) Values
nodes.rationale: Unified measure of feature importance assigning each feature an importance value for particular predictions, quantifying contribution to model output

nodes.label: Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs)
nodes.rationale: Visualizes marginal effect of one or two features on predicted outcome, averaged over effects of all other features

nodes.label: Graph Neural Network for Topological Embeddings
nodes.rationale: GraphSAGE model to generate learned topological embeddings capturing essential topological characteristics of substructures

nodes.label: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train (QITT) Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Tensor decomposition technique to compress multi-scale substructure features while extracting important information and reducing dimensionality

nodes.label: 91 Pre-computed Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Water on Functionalized Graphene
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive dataset encompassing wide range of functionalization types, surface coverages, and salt concentrations

nodes.label: 1000 Simulated Galaxy Catalogs at Redshift Zero
nodes.rationale: Large suite of simulations with unique combinations of six global parameters governing cosmology and feedback physics, comprising ~720,000 galaxies

nodes.label: 1000 Dark Matter Halo Merger Trees from Cosmological Simulations
nodes.rationale: Dataset of merger trees extracted from cosmological simulations for training and evaluating QITT-based models

nodes.label: Five-fold Range of Water Mobility in Graphene Channels
nodes.rationale: Water diffusion coefficients can be precisely tuned from 0.40×10^-5 to 1.98×10^-5 cm²/s through design parameter control

nodes.label: 10 Distinct Interfacial Water States
nodes.rationale: Unsupervised clustering identified states ranging from 'Trapped-Immobile' to 'Disordered-Mobile', linking molecular arrangements to dynamic properties

nodes.label: Salt Concentration as Most Influential Parameter for Water Transport
nodes.rationale: SHAP analysis quantitatively confirmed salt concentration is most influential, followed by carboxyl functionalization and surface coverage

nodes.label: Mass-Dependent Transition in Feedback Dominance for Black Hole Growth
nodes.rationale: Clear transition from supernova feedback dominance at low masses to AGN feedback dominance at intermediate and high masses

nodes.label: Supernova Feedback Dominates Low-Mass Galaxy Relations
nodes.rationale: A_SN1 is most influential parameter for slope, normalization, scatter, and occupation fraction in low stellar mass bin

nodes.label: AGN Feedback Dominates Intermediate and High-Mass Galaxy Relations
nodes.rationale: A_AGN1 becomes overwhelmingly dominant driver at intermediate masses, with potential sign reversal at highest masses indicating quenching

nodes.label: Remarkable Uniformity in Intermediate-Mass Galaxy Relations
nodes.rationale: Intermediate-mass bin shows almost no outliers in scaling relation parameters, indicating more robustly established relation

nodes.label: QITT-Based Models Achieve Competitive Performance for Cosmological Parameter Estimation
nodes.rationale: QITT-XGBoost significantly outperforms models using flattened combined features, highlighting benefit of QITT decomposition

nodes.label: Aggregate Features Achieve Best Performance for Omega_m Estimation
nodes.rationale: Simple baseline using global aggregate tree features achieves best performance for Omega_m, suggesting global properties are highly informative

nodes.label: Interfacial Water States Classification
nodes.rationale: Data-driven classification linking molecular arrangements to dynamic properties, from liquid-like disordered to ice-like ordered states

nodes.label: Black Hole-Galaxy Coevolution Through Feedback
nodes.rationale: Mass-dependent picture where feedback processes regulate both star formation and black hole growth across different galaxy mass scales

nodes.label: Multi-Scale Substructure Analysis of Merger Trees
nodes.rationale: Identification of significant substructures based on mass accretion rates and property changes to capture detailed formation history

nodes.label: Tensor Decomposition for Cosmological Information Extraction
nodes.rationale: Organizing substructure features into tensors and applying QITT decomposition to compress information while maintaining predictive power

nodes.label: QITT-Enhanced Multi-Scale Substructure Analysis for Cosmological Parameter Estimation
nodes.rationale: Proposes Quantum-Inspired Tensor Trains (QITT) decomposition combined with GNN-derived topological embeddings to compress and extract features from dark matter halo merger trees for cosmological parameter estimation.

nodes.label: QITT Linear Regression Model
nodes.rationale: Best performer for Ω_m prediction (RMSE 0.0246, R² 0.9231), suggesting QITT features may already linearize relationships between substructure information and cosmological parameters.

nodes.label: QITT XGBoost Model
nodes.rationale: Competitive QITT-based model (Ω_m: RMSE 0.0303, R² 0.8834; σ_8: RMSE 0.0711, R² 0.5577); significantly outperforms B4_FlatCombined_XGBoost, demonstrating QITT's effectiveness over simple flattening.

nodes.label: QITT Random Forest Model
nodes.rationale: Slightly underperforms compared to QITT_LinearRegression and QITT_XGBoost (Ω_m: RMSE 0.0320, R² 0.8696; σ_8: RMSE 0.0763, R² 0.4896).

nodes.label: B1 Aggregate Linear Regression Model
nodes.rationale: Baseline using only 11 global tree features; achieves best overall performance for Ω_m (RMSE 0.0155, R² 0.9696), indicating global merger tree properties are highly informative for this parameter.

nodes.label: B2 Raw Substructure Physical Features Linear Regression
nodes.rationale: Baseline using raw physical features without topological embeddings; yields negative R² values, indicating poor performance due to high dimensionality and noise in raw substructure features.

nodes.label: B4 Flattened Combined Features XGBoost
nodes.rationale: Baseline using same per-substructure input as QITT (physical + GNN embeddings) but flattened to 4440 features; underperforms QITT_XGBoost, demonstrating QITT's superior compression and representation.

nodes.label: Graph Neural Network Topological Embeddings
nodes.rationale: 64-dimensional embeddings generated by GNN to capture structural information from substructure graphs; t-SNE visualization shows coherence with substructure size (halo count), indicating meaningful topological encoding.

nodes.label: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Tensor decomposition method that transforms (60, 2, 37) tensor into three cores with optimal ranks (1, 2, 2, 1); compresses 4440 features to 202 QITT features while maintaining or improving predictive performance.

nodes.label: QITT Core 0 (Shape: 1×60×2)
nodes.rationale: Interfaces max_N_sub dimension (60 substructures) with first internal TT bond rank; magnitudes concentrated around zero (range -0.16 to 0.65).

nodes.label: QITT Core 1 (Shape: 2×2×2)
nodes.rationale: Small internal core with values mostly near zero but some approaching 1.0 (range -0.03 to 1.0); represents internal tensor structure.

nodes.label: QITT Core 2 (Shape: 2×37×1)
nodes.rationale: Exhibits widest range of magnitudes (-66.6 to 302.3); connects second internal TT bond rank to final feature dimension; large magnitude values suggest significant feature combinations.

nodes.label: Cosmological Parameter Ω_m (Matter Density)
nodes.rationale: Target parameter for regression; shows strong signal in global merger tree properties; best predicted by B1_Aggregate_LinearRegression (R² 0.9696).

nodes.label: Cosmological Parameter σ_8 (Matter Power Spectrum Amplitude)
nodes.rationale: Target parameter for regression; relates to amplitude of matter fluctuations; generally harder to constrain (lower R² across models); may require more subtle substructure information.

nodes.label: Dark Matter Halo Merger Trees
nodes.rationale: Dataset of 1000 trees extracted from cosmological simulations; hierarchical structures containing substructures identified by mass accretion rates and halo property changes.

nodes.label: Substructure Physical Features
nodes.rationale: Physical properties extracted for each substructure; combined with GNN topological embeddings to form per-substructure feature vectors; raw features alone perform poorly without further processing.

nodes.label: Feature Importance Analysis - QITT Random Forest
nodes.rationale: Top 20 most important features from 202 QITT-derived features; demonstrates model reliance on subset of compressed features; direct physical interpretation challenging due to complex compressed interactions.

nodes.label: Feature Importance Analysis - QITT XGBoost
nodes.rationale: Top 20 most important features from 202 QITT-derived features for XGBoost model; shows selective reliance on compressed feature subset for cosmological parameter estimation.

nodes.label: Paired t-tests for Model Comparison
nodes.rationale: Paired t-tests on squared errors of test set predictions; confirms QITT_XGBoost significantly better than B2_RawSubPhys_XGBoost and B4_FlatCombined_XGBoost; no significant difference vs B1_Aggregate_XGBoost.

nodes.label: t-SNE Projection of Topological Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Visualization of 10,000 64-dimensional GNN embeddings colored by halo count; shows diffuse clustering with coherence between embedding space regions and substructure size, indicating meaningful topological encoding.

nodes.label: Predicted vs. True Ω_m Values (QITT_XGBoost)
nodes.rationale: Scatter plot showing predictions align closely with y=x line, reflecting high R² of 0.8834; clustering around specific true values indicates model's predictive ability with some uncertainty.

nodes.label: Predicted vs. True σ_8 Values (QITT_XGBoost)
nodes.rationale: Scatter plot showing moderate correlation with greater variance in predictions compared to Ω_m, consistent with lower R² of 0.5577; indicates greater difficulty constraining this parameter.

nodes.label: Qualitative Visualization of Example Substructures
nodes.rationale: Visualization of two example substructures from merger tree; illustrates diversity in size (200 vs 12 nodes) and temporal extent (scale factor ranges); demonstrates input diversity for GNN processing.
